rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commissioned Angel of Death takes all their souls; afterward they are raised and returned to their Lord for reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذى وكل بقبض أرواحكم ثم ترجعون إلى ربكم بعد ذلك مبعوثين للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffī means taking the soul completely, as one collects a full due; here the soul means the spirit.
rows.anchor: والتوفى استبفاء النفس وهى الروح أى يقبض أرواحكم أجمعين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the earth was gathered for the Angel of Death like a basin, from which he takes souls wherever he wishes.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد حويت لملك الموت الأرض وجعلت له مثل الطست يتناول منها حيث يشاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the Angel of Death summons souls and they answer; he then orders assistants to seize them.
rows.anchor: وقيل ملك الموت يدعو الأرواح فتجيبه ثم يأمر أعوانه بقبضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the whole process and creates creatures' acts, reconciling this verse with verses saying the messengers or God take souls.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى هو الآمر لذلك كله وهو الخالق لأفعال المخلوقات وهذا وجه الجمع بين هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be to the Messenger or anyone; لو is counterfactual, with an omitted answer meaning one would see a tremendous scene.
rows.anchor: الخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو لكل أحد ولو امتناعيه والجواب محذوف أى لرايت أمرا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are those who asked whether they would really be recreated after being lost in the earth.
rows.anchor: هم الذين قالوا أئذا ضللنا فى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ refers to the future because what God promises is treated as already present; it is adverbial to ترى.
rows.anchor: ولو واذ للمضى وانما جاز ذلك لأن المترقب من الله بمنزله الموجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They bow their heads from humiliation, shame, and regret.
rows.anchor: من الذل والحياء والندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At their Lord means at His reckoning; pause here because an omitted phrase is understood: they say the following words.
rows.anchor: عند حساب ربهم ويوقف عليه لحق الحذف اذ التقدير يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They either see the truth of God's promise and threat and hear His confirmation of messengers, or say they were blind and deaf and now see and hear.
rows.anchor: صدق وعدك ووعيدك وسمعنا منك تصديق رسلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to return to worldly life and do good, meaning faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: ﴿ نعمل صالحا ﴾ أى الإيمان والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They now claim certainty about resurrection and reckoning.
rows.anchor: موقنون ﴾ بالبعث والحساب الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearer punishment is worldly punishment, including captivity and seven years of famine.
rows.anchor: عذاب الدنيا من الاسر وما محنوا به من السنة سبع سنين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the nearer punishment as humiliation and the greater one as abiding in the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن الدار انى العذاب الادنى الخذلال والعذاب الأكبر الخلود فى النيران

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the nearer punishment as the punishment of the grave.
rows.anchor: وقيل العذاب الادنى عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aim is that those punished in this life might repent of disbelief.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يرجعون ﴾ يتوبون عن الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling adopted children by their fathers' names is more just and fair in God's sight, the more equitable alternative.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط ﴾ أعدل ﴿ عند الله ﴾ وبين أن دعاءهم لآبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, a man who liked another's son adopted him, gave him a son's inheritance share, and called him by his own lineage.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل فى الجاهلية إذا أعجبه ولد الرجل ضمه إلى نفسه وجعل له مثل نصيب الذكر من أولاده من ميراثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eloquence comes from alternating connection and separation among imperative, declarative, nominal, then imperative clauses.
rows.anchor: حيث وصل الجملة الطلبية فصل الخبرية عنها ووصل بيها ثم فصل الاسمية عنها ووصل بينها ثم فصل بالطلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their fathers are unknown, there is no father to whom they can be attributed.
rows.anchor: فإن لم تعلموا لهم آباء تنسبونهم اليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are brothers and allies in religion; calling someone brother or mawla refers to religious kinship and alliance.
rows.anchor: فهم إخوانكم فى الدين وأولياؤكم فى الدين فقالوا هذا أخى وهذا مولاى ويا أخى ويامولاى

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mistaken attribution through ignorance before prohibition is not sinful; deliberate attribution afterward is. The rule covers adoption error and intent.
rows.anchor: أى لا اثم عليكم فيما فعلتموه من ذلك مخطئين جاهلين قبل ورود النهى

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in the second clause may be genitive, coordinated with the earlier ما.
rows.anchor: وما فى موضع الجر عطف على ما الأولى

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: For an adoptee of unknown lineage younger than the adopter, lineage is established and an enslaved person freed; if older, lineage is not established but emancipation still occurs.
rows.anchor: وإذا وجد التبنى فان كان المتبنى مجهول النسب وأصغر سنامنه ثبت نسبه منه وعتق ان كان عبدا له وان كان أكبر سنامنه لم يثبت النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adoption cannot establish lineage for someone of known lineage, though an enslaved adoptee is freed.
rows.anchor: وأما المعروف النسب فلا يثبت نسبه بالتبنى وعتق ان كان عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not hold people accountable for mistakes and accepts repentance from those who acted deliberately.
rows.anchor: لا يؤاخذكم بالخطأ ويقبل التوبة من المتعمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can be fulfilled by saying, O God, bless Muhammad, or May God bless Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أى قولوا اللهم صل على محمد أو صلى الله على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salutation means asking God to grant Muhammad peace, or submitting fully to his command and judgment.
rows.anchor: أى قولوا اللهم سلم على محمد أو انقادوا لامره وحكمه انقيادا

rows.speaker: محمد ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet said two angels are assigned to him: when a Muslim blesses him they ask God to forgive that person and God says amen; if not, they pray against the person and God again says amen.
rows.anchor: وسئل عليه السلام عن هذه الآية فقال إن الله وكل بى ملكين فلا أذكر عند عبد مسلم فيصلى على إلا قال ذانك الملكان غفر الله لك

rows.speaker: الطحاوي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭaḥāwī holds that invoking blessings on the Prophet is obligatory once.
rows.anchor: ثم هى واجبة مرة عند الطحاوى

rows.speaker: الكرخي
rows.claim: Al-Karkhī holds that the blessing is obligatory whenever the Prophet's name is mentioned.
rows.anchor: وكلما ذكر اسمه عند الكرخى وهو الاحتياط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking blessings whenever the Prophet is mentioned is precautionary and the view of the majority.
rows.anchor: كلما ذكر اسمه عند الكرخى وهو الاحتياط وعليه الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no objection to including the Prophet's family when blessings are sent upon him.
rows.anchor: وان صلى على غيره على سبيل التبع كقوله صلى الله على النبى وآله فلا كلام فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Separately invoking blessings on another member of the Prophet's household is disliked and, in Nasafi's polemic, a distinctive practice of the Rāfiḍīs.
rows.anchor: وأما اذا أفرد غيره من أهل البيت بالصلاة فمكروه وهو من شعائر الروافض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks who provides, then answers for them that God does: they inwardly admit it but refuse to say so because this entails worshipping the provider, not powerless idols.
rows.anchor: أمره بأن يقررهم بقوله من يرزقكم ثم أمره بأن يتولى الاجابة والاقرار عنهم بقوله يرزقكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acknowledging that God provides exposes the inconsistency of worshipping beings unable to provide.
rows.anchor: لزمهم أن يقال لهم فمالكم لا تعبدون من يرزقكم وتؤثرون عليه من لا يقدر على الرزق

words: وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This fair-minded formulation says one faction, monotheists or polytheists, is guided and the other astray; even an opponent recognizes its fairness.
rows.anchor: وهذا من الكلام المنصف الذى كل من سمعه من موال أو مناف قال لمن خوطب به قد أنصفك صاحبك

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding proof subtly indicates which side is guided; indirectness better achieves the debater's aim.
rows.anchor: وفى درجة بعد تقدم ما قدم من التقرير دلالة غير خفية على من هومن الفريقين على الهدى ومن هو فى الضلال المبين ولكن التعريض أوصل بالمجادل إلى الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different prepositions picture the guided person riding a fine horse and the misguided person submerged in darkness, unable to see where to go.
rows.anchor: لأن صاحب الهدى كانه مستعل على فرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is more fair-minded: the wording assigns crime to the speakers and action to their audience, pairing censured wrongdoing with praised, commanded deeds.
rows.anchor: هذا أدخل فى الانصاف من الأول حيث أسند الاجرام إلى المخاطبين وهو مزجور عنه محظور والعمل إلى المخاطبين وهو مأمور به مشكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones invoked are idols, and as inanimate objects they cannot hear prayers.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن تدعوهم ﴾ أى الاصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they could hear, the idols would not answer, since they do not claim divinity and disavow it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولو سمعوا ﴾ على سبيل الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day idols will disown their association and worship, saying their worshippers did not worship them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ﴾ باشراككم لهم وعبادتكم اياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No informant explains these causes of delusion like God, who knows hidden matters; the expert alone tells the truth, and God is expert here.
rows.anchor: ولا يخبرك بالأمر مخبر هو مثل خبير عالم به يريدان الخبير بالأمر وحده هو الذى يخبرك بالحقيقة

rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nūn says creatures need God in every breath, thought, and moment, because their existence and continuance depend on Him.
rows.anchor: قال ذو النون الخلق محتاجون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are called poor not to demean them but to direct them toward dependence; God is independent of all things.
rows.anchor: ولم يسمهم بالفقراء للتحقير بل للتعريض على الاستغناء ولهذا وصف نفسه بالغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is praised by every tongue; His riches benefit creation because He gives generously, and beneficiaries praise their benefactor.
rows.anchor: المحمود بكل لسان ولم يسمهم بالفقراء للتحقير بل للتعريض على الاستغناء

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says self-sufficiency veils a person, while displaying need brings one to God; inward dependence and cutting off from others make servitude pure, whose sign is asking no one.
rows.anchor: قال سهل لما خلق الله الخلق حكم لنفسه بالغنى ولهم بالفقر فمن ادعى الغنى حجب عن الله

rows.speaker: الواسطى
rows.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says whoever finds sufficiency through God is not poor, and whoever is ennobled through God is not abased.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطى من استغنى بالله لا يفتقر ومن تعزز بالله لا يذل

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says God-given richness corresponds to need: the more dependent a servant becomes, the richer he becomes.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسين على مقدار افتقار العبد إلى الله يكون غنيا بالله وكلما ازداد افتقارا ازداد غنى

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yaḥyā says poverty is better than wealth because it brings humility and wealth pride; returning humbly to God is better than returning with multiplied deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى الفقر خير للعبد من الغنى لأن المذلة فى الفقر والكبر فى الغنى والرجوع إلى الله بالتواضع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view lists three marks of saints: trust in God, need of Him, and returning to Him, each in everything.
rows.anchor: وقيل صفة الأولياء ثلاثة الثقة بالله في كل شيء والفقر إليه في كل شيء والرجوع إليه من كل شىء

rows.speaker: الشبلى
rows.claim: Al-Shiblī says poverty draws affliction, and all the affliction it brings is honor.
rows.anchor: وقال الشبلى الفقر يجر البلاء وبلاؤه كله عز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening إذ is in apposition to the earlier إذ in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذ ﴾ بدل من اذ الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus sent two messengers by God's command, named Ṣādiq and Ṣadūq; they met Ḥabīb al-Najjār tending sheep, who asked about their mission and signs.
rows.anchor: أى أرسل عيسى بأمرنا ﴿ اثنين ﴾ صادقا وصدوقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers said they healed the sick and cured the blind and leper; Ḥabīb's sick son rose after their touch, many others were healed, and the news spread.
rows.anchor: فقالا نحن رسولا عيسى ندعوكم من عبادة الأوثان إلى عبادة الرحمن فقال أمعكما آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the king questioned the pair and they were beaten or imprisoned, Jesus sent Simon, who entered in disguise and gained the royal household's trust.
rows.anchor: وقيل حبسا ثم بعث عيسى شمعون فدخل متنكرا وعاشر حاشية الملك حتى استأنسوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simon prompted the king to test them; God restored a blind boy's sight and revived one dead seven days, who warned of the Fire and described a heavenly intercessor for the three.
rows.anchor: فدعوا بغلام مات من سبعة أيام فقام وقال إنى أدخلت فى سبعة أودية من النار لما مت عليه من الشرك وأنا أحذركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king admitted his idols could neither hear, see, harm, nor benefit; he, Simon, and the messengers believed, while Gabriel's cry destroyed the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ليس لى عنك سر ان إلهنا لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يضر ولا ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the town rejected the two messengers.
rows.anchor: فكذب أصحاب القرية الرسولين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr's reading relates the verb to ʿazza yaʿuzzu, meaning to overcome; God thereby overpowered and subdued the opponents.
rows.anchor: فعززنا أبو بكر من عزه يعزه إذا غلبه أى فغلبنا وقهرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object is omitted to focus on Simon as the means of support and the subtle strategy that made truth prevail and falsehood fall.
rows.anchor: وترك ذكر المفعول به لأن المراد ذكر المعزز به وهو شمعون وما لطف فيه من التدبير حتى عز الحق وذل الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three messengers together addressed the town's people, saying they had been sent to them.
rows.anchor: أى قال الثلاثة لأهل القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the messengers a bad omen because they dislike their religion; ignorant people treat what they like as auspicious and what they hate as unlucky.
rows.anchor: تشاءمنا بكم وذلك أنهم كرهوا دينهم ونفرت منه نفوسهم وعادة الجهال أن يتيمنوا بكل شىء مالوا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people blame an unwanted event on ill fortune or credit a welcome event to a good omen.
rows.anchor: ويتشاءموا بما نفروا عنه وكرهوه فإن أصابهم بلاء أو نعمة قالوا بشؤم هذا وبركة ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that rain had been withheld, prompting their accusation.
rows.anchor: وقيل حبس عنهم المطر فقالوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat to stone them can mean killing, expelling, or insulting them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لنرجمنكم ﴾ لنقتلنكم أو لنطردنكم أو لنشتمنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The painful punishment threatened is the Fire, the most severe punishment.
rows.anchor: وليصيبنكم عذاب النار وهو أشد عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drop is filthy fluid emitted from the urethra, the channel of impurity.
rows.anchor: مذرة خارجة من الاحليل الذى هو قناه النجاسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though from a lowly origin, a person openly disputes with his Lord and denies the power to revive decayed bones, the sort of lifeless matter from which he came.
rows.anchor: فهو على مهانة أصله ودناءة أوله يتصدى لمخاصمة ربه وينكر قدرته على إحياء الميت بعد مارمت عظامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His denial is extreme stubbornness: he disputes resurrection from dead matter despite himself originating from lifeless matter.
rows.anchor: ثم يكون خصامه فى ألزم وصف له وألصقه به وهو كونه منشأ من موات وهو ينكر انشاءه من موات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objector made his example by crumbling a bone.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وضرب لنا مثلا ﴾ بفته العظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He forgot that God first created him from semen, a more remarkable origin than reviving bone.
rows.anchor: من المنى فهو أغرب من إحياء العظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun is annexed to its object: God created him.
rows.anchor: المصدر مضاف إلى المفعول أى خلقنا إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramīm is a noun for decayed bones rather than an adjective such as ramma or rufāt.
rows.anchor: هو اسم لما بلى من العظام غير صفة كالرمة والرفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ramīm is a noun it is not made feminine, though it is predicated of the feminine noun bones.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لم يؤنث وقد وقع خبر المؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some who say life inhabits bones and death makes carrion bones impure cite this verse; Nasafi holds bones, hair, and sinews pure because life does not inhabit them and death does not affect them.
rows.anchor: ومن يثبت الحياة فى العظام ويقول إن عظام الميتة نجسة لأن الموت يؤثر فيها من قبل أن الحياة تحلها يتشبث بهذه الآية وهى عندنا طاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving the bones means restoring them to their former fresh, moist state within a living, sensing body.
rows.anchor: والمراد باحياء العظام فى الآية ردها إلى ما كانت عليه غضة رطبة فى بدن حى حساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anshaʾahā means created them, and the first time means their initial creation.
rows.anchor: خلقها ﴿ أول مرة ﴾ أى ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here khalq means every created thing.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهو بكل خلق ﴾ مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every creature's parts, even dispersed across land and sea, and gathers and restores them as before.
rows.anchor: لا تخفى عليه أجزاؤه وان تفرقت فى البر والبحر فيجمعه ويعيده كما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they wondered that a warner had come to them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وعجبوا أن جاءهم ﴾ من أن جاءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warner is a messenger from among them sent to warn them; they found it implausible that the Prophet was human.
rows.anchor: رسول من أنفسهم بنذرهم يعنى استبعدوا أن يكون النبى من البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them disbelievers rather than simply they expresses anger and shows only hardened unbelievers would dare this claim.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل وقالوا إظهار للغضب عليهم ودلالة على أن هذا القول لا يجسر عليه إلا الكافرون المتوغلون فى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call one God confirmed a liar and magician, marvel at monotheistic truth, yet fail to marvel at false polytheism; no disbelief is more extreme.
rows.anchor: إذ لا كفر أبلغ من أن يسموا من صدقه الله كاذبا ساحرا ويتعجبوا من التوحيد وهو الحق الأبلج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after ʿUmar became Muslim, twenty-five Quraysh leaders pressed Abū Ṭālib to make the Prophet renounce them and their idols; he offered a word that would give them Arab rule and non-Arab submission, and they rejected it.
rows.anchor: وروى أن عمر رضى الله عنه لما أسلم فرح به المؤمنون وشق على قريش فاجتمع خمسة وعشرون نفسا من صناديدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjāb means extraordinarily wondrous, emphatic in its wonder.
rows.anchor: أى أصير ان هذا الشيء عجاب أى بليغ فى العجب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation distinguishes ʿajīb, something with a counterpart, from ʿujāb, something without one.
rows.anchor: وقيل العجيب ماله مثل والعجاب مالا مثل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet's decisive answer silenced them at Abū Ṭālib's gathering, Quraysh's leaders left and spoke among themselves.
rows.anchor: وانطلق أشراف قريش عن مجلس أبي طالب بعد ما بكتهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالجواب العتيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن means أي, since people leaving a disputation are expected to discuss what happened; their departure implies speech.
rows.anchor: وأن بمعنى أى لأن المنطلقين عن مجلس التقاول لابد لهم من أن يتكلموا ويتفاوضوا فيما جرى لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their instruction is to persist in worshipping their idols.
rows.anchor: ﴿ واصبروا على ﴾ عبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God wills and decrees this affair, so it cannot be repelled and patience is their only recourse.
rows.anchor: أى يريده الله تعالى ويحكم بامضائه فلا مرد له ولا ينفع فيه إلا الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they mean a calamity of time is destined for them and cannot be escaped.
rows.anchor: أو أن هذا الأمر لشىء من نوائب الدهر يراد بنا فلا انفكاك لنا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they had not heard of is monotheism.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما سمعنا بهذا ﴾ التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the last religion to mean Christianity, latest among religious communities, whose adherents are trinitarian rather than unitarian.
rows.anchor: فى ملة عيسى التى هى آخر الملل لأن النصارى مثلثة غير موحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they mean Quraysh's religion inherited from their fathers.
rows.anchor: أو فى ملة قريش التى أدركنا عليها آباءنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the claim a lie fabricated by Muhammad himself.
rows.anchor: كذب اختلقه محمد من تلقاء نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expanded the person's heart for Islam, enabling guidance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره ﴾ أى وسع صدره

rows.speaker: محمد ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet said light entering a heart expands it; its sign is longing for the eternal home, turning from delusion, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: وسئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الشرح فقال إذا دخل النور القلب انشرح وانفسح فقيل فهل لذلك من علامة قال نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being on light from one's Lord means having clarity and insight.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فهو على نور من ربه ﴾ بيان وبصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison asks whether the guided person is like one whose heart is sealed and hardened; it is omitted because the following warning implies it.
rows.anchor: المعنى أفمن شرح الله صدره فاهتدى كمن طبع على قلبه فقسا قلبه فحذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من may mean their hearts harden from abandoning God's remembrance, or because remembrance and His signs make them harder, as in the verse about added defilement.
rows.anchor: من ترك ذكر الله أو من أجل ذكر الله أى إذا ذكر الله عندهم أو آياته ازدادت قلوبهم قساوة كقوله فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those people are in manifest error.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولئك في ضلال مبين ﴾ غواية ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making God's name the subject, or foregrounding it with نزل, magnifies the excellence of the revealed discourse.
rows.anchor: فى ايقاع اسم الله مبتدا أو بناء نزل عليه تفخيم لأحسن الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتابا may be an appositive to أحسن الحديث or a circumstantial accusative describing it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كتابا ﴾ بدل من أحسن الحديث أو حال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's parts resemble one another in truth, clarity, admonition, wisdom, inimitability, and more.
rows.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا فى الصدق والبيان والوعظ والحكمة والاعجاز وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathānī means repeated: stories, reports, rulings, commands, prohibitions, promises, warnings, and admonitions recur, explaining the book's resemblance.
rows.anchor: جمع مثنى بمعنى مردد ومكرر لما ثنى من قصصه وأنبائه وأحكامه وأوامره ونواهيه ووعده ووعيده ومواعظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Quran is repeated in recitation and therefore does not become tiresome.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنه يثنى فى التلاوة فلا يمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular book takes a plural description because it is a whole made of many details, as one calls the Quran portions, suras, and verses.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاز وصف الواحد بالجمع لأن الكتاب جملة ذات تفاصيل وتفاصيل الشىء هى جملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, مثاني is specification of متشابها, meaning recurring features resemble one another, like a man's many beautiful qualities.
rows.anchor: أو منصوب على التمييز من متشابها كما تقول رأيت رجلا حسنا شمائل والمعنى متشابهة مثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The skin trembles and moves; the verb describes its intense contraction.
rows.anchor: ﴿ تقشعر ﴾ تضطرب وتتحرك

words: تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing the Quran's warnings makes those who fear God experience awe and gooseflesh.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعوا بالقرآن وبآيات وعيده أصابتهم خشية تقشعر منها جلودهم

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says when a believer's skin shudders from fear of God, sins fall like leaves from a dry tree.
rows.anchor: وفى الحديث إذا اقشعر جلد المؤمن من خشية الله تحاتت عنا ذنوبه كما يتحات عن الشجرة اليابسة ورقها

words: ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When mercy verses are mentioned, skin and hearts soften and fear recedes; إلى conveys settling toward remembrance.
rows.anchor: أى إذا ذكرت آيات الرحمة لانت جلودهم وقلوبهم وزال عنها ما كان بها من الخشية والقشعريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلى is used because لين takes on the sense of a verb governing إلى: they become calm toward remembrance.
rows.anchor: وعدى بالى لتضمنه معنى فعل متعد بالى كانه قيل اطمأنت إلى ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy is not named after remembrance because God's mercy precedes His anger, so remembering Him evokes compassion.
rows.anchor: واقتصر على ذكر الله من غير ذكر الرحمة لأن رحمته سبقت غضبه فلا صالة رحمته إذا ذكر الله لم يخطر بالبال إلا كونه رؤوفا رحيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Skin is mentioned first alone, then with hearts, because the heart is the locus of fear and was already implied.
rows.anchor: وذكرت الجلود وحدها أولا ثم قرنت بها القلوب ثانيا لأن محل الخشية القلب فكان ذكرها يتضمن ذكر القلوب

words: ذَٰلِكَ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهْدِى بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to the Book; God guides by it those He knows will choose guidance.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ذلك ﴾ اشارة إلى الكتاب وهو ﴿ هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates misguidance in whomever He leads astray, who then has no guide to truth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن يضلل الله ﴾ يخلق الضلالة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted comparison asks whether someone shielding himself with his face is like one safe from punishment.
rows.anchor: كمن أمن من العذاب فحذف الخبر كما حذف فى نظائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the severity of punishment.
rows.anchor: وسوء العذاب شدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People shield their precious face with a hand; one thrown into Hell has hands bound to the neck and can shield himself only with his face.
rows.anchor: والذى يلقى فى النار يلقى مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه فلا يتهيأ له أن يتقى النار إلا بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are the keepers of Hell, addressing wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: أن تقول لهم خزنة النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they are told to taste is the recompense of what they earned.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ما كنتم تكسبون ﴾ أى كسبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza applied to a negative affirms and confirms that God suffices.
rows.anchor: أدخلت همزة الانكار على كلمة النفي فأفيد معنى اثبات الكفاية وتقريرها

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads the plural عباده, referring to the prophets and believers.
rows.anchor: عباده حمزة وعلى أي الأنبياء والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the singular reading, God's servant is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ﴿ عبده ﴾ أي محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This resembles God's assurance that He has sufficed the Prophet against the mockers.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل انا كفيناك المستهزئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh said they feared their idols would make the Messenger mad or harm him because he criticized them.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن قريشا قالت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انا نخاف أن تخبلك آلهتنا وانا نخشى عليك مضرتها لعيبك إياها

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone God leads astray has no guide.
rows.anchor: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalanāhu means giving a favor gratuitously, without compensation.
rows.anchor: أى أعطيناه تفضلا يقال خولنى إذا أعطاك على غير جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not pause after from Us because the response to إذا is the following verb, he said.
rows.anchor: ولا تقف عليه لأن جواب إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may mean the favor came from their excellence and merit, or from their knowledge of earning, as Qarun claimed.
rows.anchor: منى أنى سأعطاه لما فى من فضل واستحقاق أو على علم منى بوجوه الكسب كما قال قارون على علم عندى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine suffix refers to the favor by meaning, as نعمة منا denotes a thing or portion of favor; alternatively, ما in إنما is relative and the suffix refers to it.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر الضمير فى أوتيته وهو للنعمة نظرا إلى المعنى لأن قوله نعمة منا شيئا من النعمة وقسما منها وقيل ما فى إنما موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correction rebukes their claim: the favor is a trial of gratitude or ingratitude.
rows.anchor: انكار له كأنه قال ما خولناك من النعمة لما تقول بل هى فتنة أى ابتلاء وامتحان لك أتشكر أم تكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine predicate فتنة permits a feminine subject; the alternate reading follows the masculine reference to ما.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الخبر مؤنثا أعنى فتنة ساغ تأنيث المبتدا لأجله

rows.speaker: قارئ
rows.claim: An alternate reading has هو فتنة, following the masculine reference in إنما أوتيته.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بل هو فتنة على وفق إنما أوتيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not know that the favor is a trial.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون ﴾ أنها فتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāء marks this as a result of their earlier recoil when God alone is mentioned: in distress they call Him, not the idols they welcome.
rows.anchor: والسبب فى عطف هذه الآية بالفاء وعطف مثلها فى أول السورة بالواو أن هذه وقعت مسببة عن قوله وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intervening verses are an aside reinforcing the rebuke through the Prophet's supplication and the severe warning.
rows.anchor: وما بينهما من الآى اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first occurrence in the sūra uses واو because its clause merely follows a related clause; فاء here signals causation.
rows.anchor: وأما الآية الأولى فلم تقع مسببة وما هى إلا جملة ناسبت جملة قبلها فعطفت عليها بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast says a believer's distress leads him to God, while the disbeliever also turns to God, as if his disbelief were treated as belief in this appeal.
rows.anchor: ثم تقول زيد كافر بالله فاذا مسه ضر التجأ إليه فتجىء بالفاء مجيئك بها ثمة كأن الكافر حين التجأ إلى الله التجاء المؤمن إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following threat applies to all wrongdoers if general, or specifically to these people; even all worldly wealth could not ransom them from punishment.
rows.anchor: وقوله ولو أن للذين ظلموا متناول لهم ولكل ظالم إن جعل عاما أو إياهم خاصة إن عنينهم به كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to the claim that the favor was given because of one's own knowledge.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قد قالها ﴾ هذه المقالة وهى قوله إنما أوتيته على علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One identification is Qarun and his people, who made the claim and approved of it among themselves.
rows.anchor: أى قارون وقومه حيث قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندى وقومه راضون بها فكأنهم قالوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, other earlier nations may have made the same claim.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون فى الأمم الخالية آخرون قائلون مثلها

words: فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly possessions and what they amassed did not benefit them.
rows.anchor: من متاع الدنيا وما يجمعون منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are driven violently, like prisoners or rebels taken to imprisonment or execution.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم ﴾ سوقا عنيفا كما يفعل بالاسارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zumar is a circumstantial accusative meaning separate groups following one another.
rows.anchor: ﴿ زمرا ﴾ حال أي افواجا متفرقة بعضها في اثر بعض

rows.speaker: كوفى
rows.claim: Kufan reciters use the lighter form of the opening verb in both passages about Hell's gates.
rows.anchor: ﴿ حتى إذا جاؤوها فتحت ﴾ بالتخفيف فيهماكوفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell has seven gates.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أبوابها ﴾ وهي سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's keepers are angels assigned to punish its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أي حفظة جهنم وهم الملائكة الموكلون بتعذيب اهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers were from among humanity, the children of Adam.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ألم يأتكم رسل منكم ﴾ من بني ادم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting your day means the time of entering Hell, not the Day of Resurrection itself.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا ﴾ أي وقتكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They affirm that messengers came and recited God's verses to them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قالوا بلى ﴾ اتونا وتلوا علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sentence to fill Hell took effect because of their evil deeds; they recall disbelief and error as the cause.
rows.anchor: وجبت علينا كلمة الله لاملأن جهنم بسوء اعمالنا كما قالوا غلبت علينا شقوتنا وكنا قوما ضالين
